utterances.text: Moving on then into early 1993, did you see more of them? Say, in the first two or three months of 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in Travnik. Not in the town of Travnik. That battalion of ours was already in existence. It was part of the 7th Muslim Brigade, and it had its headquarters in Zenica. And the atmosphere was such that the organs of power, or rather, through cooperating with the organs of power, wanted to have the minimum number of uniformed individuals in the town. But outside of my zone of responsibility -- everything I could say would just be guesswork. In the Biljana area and the area of Zenica and other areas I would say would just be guesswork. I've already seen this video. It was shown on a political programme. I saw it quite recently.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, you just mentioned "outside of your zone of responsibility," and I have a couple of questions about that. Were there areas that you were aware of, that you had knowledge of, that had a high concentration of foreign soldiers in Central Bosnia in the early part of 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. A high concentration of foreign combatants? No. No. A high concentration; well, that really reminds one of the formation of brigades, divisions, et cetera. I mentioned what we had. We had the zones of responsibility for the 306th, the 312th, the 17th Krajina, the 7th Battalion. You know, those were the forces in Travnik. But as to everything else you're asking me about, I could try to guess about these matters, but it goes beyond that conflict, beyond the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No, I'm not asking you to guess, sir. I'm wondering if -- rather than focussing on brigades or divisions or large units like that, were you aware of or did you have personal knowledge of specific locations where there were, say, company-sized or even platoon-sized groups of foreign soldiers in Central Bosnia in the early part of 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll be frank: The first information I had about the existence of such a unit came from UNPROFOR. The liaison officers often came to my command post and provided the -- and provided me with information. So that, as far as this El Mujahed unit was concerned, I don't know how that would be translated, which would say deployed in the area of Biljana, in the Travnik Municipality, or to be more specific, in Mehurici, liaison officers from UNPROFOR, from BritBat, would often contact me, and they were interested in the activities of these combatants. They weren't active in my brigade's zone of responsibility. I didn't know much about them. So there was such a unit in the area I have just mentioned, in the Mehurici area. As to the strength of that unit, as to how it was equipped, et cetera, I have no information. I didn't have any information about that at the time. And likewise, I don't know under whose command this unit was. It certainly wasn't linked to the army. But I don't want to start answering other questions that you are surely going to put to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, were you -- did you have knowledge of any foreign combatants operating within your area of responsibility, within areas controlled by the 312th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, as I have already said. In my area, in my zone, in my brigade's zone of combat operations, no such foreign combatants were present. I have information according to which they never appeared there, because my battalion commanders would inform me, and I saw in the conflict, the aggression and the entire situation in Bosnia-Herzegovina from a different perspective, as well as what we had to fight for because we didn't have any other state. I didn't need anyone else's -- I didn't need anyone's assistance. My idea is quite different. I didn't need anyone's assistance. We had enough forces. I perhaps needed weapons at the time, but not men who would fight for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You told us, sir, about receiving information from UNPROFOR and BritBat. And among the things they told you about was, as you put it, the El Mujahed unit in Mehurici. Other than -- other than -- those international military personnel, did you have any other knowledge coming from other sources about this unit in Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I mentioned the impossibility of having communications in the case of command and control, when we're talking about the 3rd Corps and the subordinate brigades, and I had one of those brigades. There were operations groups that were formed. So in Travnik itself, the OG Bosanska Krajina was active. It was headed by the late General Alagic. On a number of occasions at briefings, I heard from the late Alagic that he had problems with people who claimed to be the El Mujahed. They would not obey and carry out orders. That's supposed to be just one command, the oldest command in the town and in the zone that the OG Bosanska Krajina had at the time. There were problems all the time. At least, this is what I found out from Commander Alagic. These people were people or groups who were not obedient. They didn't want to place themselves under anyone else's command. And because of a certain code of conduct that they had, they wanted to wage a war in the way that they thought was most appropriate. They wanted to decide whether they were go into combat on any given day or whether they would simply not go into combat. This is what I heard from Alagic, and there were quite a few problems. They didn't want to be placed under anyone's command. These were the forces that were present in that area. As to whether they engaged in combat or not, I do not know. I had problems of my own. So sometimes I was sorry for the fact that the commander had to deal with problems that shouldn't have been his, but that was a problem that was present. It was a cancer that was present in his zone of combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, you've used the term "code of conduct" several times. And I'm wondering if you can perhaps elaborate or explain to the Trial Chamber what exactly you mean by the use of that phrase "code of conduct."

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, I've never read it. But I have heard of its existence. I know that such a code existed within such forces that had been established. As to the contents of this code, I don't know. It is only my assumption that it involved religious matters as well. But I couldn't tell you more than that because I really haven't read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, this code of conduct, this document or pamphlet or booklet or whatever, does that go by the title "Instructions for the Muslim Fighter"?

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I really don't know. I was not familiar with such literature at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence is on their feet, but the witness has already said he didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Since the witness has already given the answer, there is no need to react.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, I have just a couple of questions. It was unclear to me earlier when you spotted Mr. Mektauf on the videotape the time period when I first met him or first knew him. Can you tell us, please, when you first met this individual and roughly what year or time period.

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1991 in August, after I had arrived from the former JNA, and since a cousin of mine worked in his video club - she issued videotapes - I went to see her, and it was on that occasion that I met her boss.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Caber.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions at this time, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will have a break in about five minutes. I just have a few questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The boss of your cousin, Mr. Mektauf, do you know where he is at the moment? Do you know what his whereabouts are currently?

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know. I learned through the media that he is in detention in Sarajevo and that proceedings are currently underway against him. Whether he's only a suspect or already an accused, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And you don't know anything about the charges against him.

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be perfectly frank, Your Honour, I know only what I was able to hear on the TV.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What did they say on TV?

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: On TV, I heard that it is because of the fact that certain individuals were taken away from Travnik and detained in locations which were known only to him. So cases of disappearances of certain individuals including a number of deaths. That's what I heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A moment ago when answering a question that was put to you by the Prosecutor, you mentioned a briefing with General Alagic, and you said that he had told you that he had had problems with these foreigners, and you also indicated that they did not obey orders, and that they were causing problems. Does that mean that it is possible that these elements participated together with the BH Army forces in certain military actions?

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably because of what I had already said with relation to Mr. Alagic and the problems he experienced with such individuals it would have never occurred to him to link the army with those forces. Because from what he told me, it seems that they refused to obey orders. That is the only knowledge that I have about these units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Does that mean if they refuse to obey orders, that it is possible that they had been asked to take part in military actions?

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, before any troops can be used for military actions, combat actions, such troops need to be placed under certain command. As far as I remember, they refused to be placed under the command of General Alagic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the videoclip that we saw a moment ago, dating from the month of August 1992, people were wearing summer clothes in the video. We also saw a number of young soldiers equipped, dressed up. We also saw a coat of arms or a sleeve band on the right arm of one of them. I'm referring to the individual who was next to Mektauf. Now, these soldiers, in your opinion, what were they doing there and where had they come from?

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The soldiers whom we were able to see lined up wearing uniforms, I can only assume that they were linked to the area of Travnik, or perhaps even a greater area, the area of Bosanska Krajina, because we had able-bodied young men who had arrived in a convoy from that area. So those would have been these young soldiers. And again, I have to go back to what I earlier said: They became members of a formation that they considered to be adequate for them. They never joined any TO units or the brigade, but they joined these Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your headquarters were located in the vicinity. In your opinion, where were they quartered? Because after all, there were several dozens of them. They must have been quartered somewhere. Where?

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, my assumption is that some of them were located in Medresa, or rather, the religious school which I talked about a moment ago. And that the remainder were deployed in the area in the vicinity of the front line against the Serbs because, after all, we were in August 1992. And as far as I can recall, elements of these forces were located in the area to the northwest of Turbe, in Karaula. The name of the location is Radalj, and there was also Ukalj. So it was in the area towards Serb forces. Rotations carried out in the area, and probably those who were located in the religious school went there. There was Territorial Defence staff located in the area, and they must have facilitated the passage of these units. So these units were rotated because it was necessary to act jointly against Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The date is the 21st of August. It must have been in the afternoon because of the shades. The sun was behind the soldiers. So this probably took place in the afternoon. Which was the military authority that had the supreme power in Travnik? Which was the military authority that was present in Travnik at the highest level that could actually issue permission for such a military ceremony to take place in Travnik in presence of a number of civilians and religious authorities, and also someone who spoke on the megaphone whom we could not hear, but who obviously was holding a kind of rally? Who was the military authority that was able to organise such a gathering, such a rally?

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. The highest command at the time in Travnik was the Territorial Defence staff headed by a commander. Whether permission was indeed issued to that effect, I don't know. Moreover, I was not aware of that rally. I was not aware of this inspection of ranks at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the last question before the break: What is the name of the commander of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The TO commander after me, from the 1st of June until the formation of the brigades, that is, the month of November was Mr. Haso Ribo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But on the day this rally was held, you were responsible; you were in charge of the TO.

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, Your Honour. I stated that I had been commander of the Territorial Defence until the end of May 1992. After that, I was the TO chief of staff from the 1st of June 1992 until the time when the brigades were established. That period of time was covered by Mr. Haso Ribo. He was the commander of the Territorial Defence, and I was the chief of staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So on that day when this video was filmed, you were the chief of staff.

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are going to have a recess and come back at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We are going to resume with the hearing. I have just one final question for you, Witness. After that, I will give the floor to the Defence if they wish to ask any additional questions to you. You have spoken this afternoon about OG Zapad, and in that context, you also mentioned OG Bosanska Krajina. I should like to know what operational group exactly you were part of. Before you give your answer, let me just tell you that documents have been tendered by the Defence according to which you received orders from General Alagic. In particular, I am referring to the document which states that the 312th Brigade was one of the addressees just as the 17th Krajina and the 306th Brigade. I'm referring to the document 1005. This document, therefore, says that you were part of the group which was led by Alagic. Could you now tell us precisely who was your superior before the 3rd Corps, because we have this operational group as well.

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was speaking about the difficulties that the commander of the 3rd Corps was faced with in connection with command and control with a large number of lower units, including brigades. And it is with that objective in mind that the Operational Group Zapad and Operational Group Bosanska Krajina were established in March and April in 1993. My command, the command of the 312th Brigade -- or rather, the whole of the brigade, was part of the OG Zapad pursuant to that order, which was located in Bugojno, whose headquarters were located in Bugojno. All my reporting activities and also in terms of receiving orders from the operational group went in that direction, and the other way around, of course. However, when combat activities started against HVO as well, there occurred an interruption in communication in terms of command and control. And in that sense, the 312th Brigade, not on its own but because there was a higher command with headquarters in Travnik, the Operational Group Bosanska Krajina which was linked to the 3rd Corps, received tasks and reported also to the Operational Group Bosanska Krajina. I cannot recall whether there was a specific order of the 3rd Corps to that effect, that that is how things should be done. But it is my assessment as a soldier that that was how it was done, that there were communications, obviously, with the Operational Group Zapad in Bugojno. But we also received tasks from the Bosanska Krajina Operational Group. And we also received orders from that group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you're now confirming that you were also under the authority of General Alagic?

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We have Exhibit 304, which is part of the record. General Alagic is the author of the document, and he described the situation in Travnik, and he indicated, concerning the unit under your command, that you were faced with Chetniks and that you had 270 men under your command and that you were placed in Travnik. It's a document dating from the 13th of April. So if that is what General Alagic said, he then believed that he had under his command 304, 312th, the 17th, the 7th Battalion, and the 306th Brigade. I have no further questions for you -- well, I would have -- we would have additional questions for you, but because of the time constraints, we cannot address everything. You are the only military commander who has appeared so far before the Chamber and who has been able to speak about the BH army. There may be other issues as well, but we might raise them with other witnesses. Time flies, and we just have 50 minutes left for questions, if any, by the Defence. Let me now give the floor to the Defence to see if there are any questions that have arisen as a result of the questions asked by the Chamber -- or rather, by myself since my colleagues did not have anything to ask.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. I do have additional questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Caber, in response to a question put to you by my learned colleague you clarified that Commander Hadzihasanovic paid two visits to Travnik and in turn you visited Zenica on two occasions, and you met Commander Hadzihasanovic on one of those occasions. And on the other occasion, you met with the chief of staff, Mr. Mekic. In connection with that, could you please tell us the following: Were other members of the command of the 3rd Corps acting pursuant to their assignments, their tasks, and did they also pay visits to your brigade as part of their duties -- the duties that they had as members of the command of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to the answer that you gave me yesterday, that is, that the command issued you orders, that you sent them reports, and that members of the command would visit you to verify that the orders were indeed carried out. So in addition to the visit by Commander Hadzihasanovic, I would like to know whether other members of the command of the 3rd Corps came to see you, and if so, with what specific assignments.

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: So let me repeat: Yes, responsible officers from the command of the 3rd Corps did visit us in connection with a number of issues such as combat readiness of troops facing Serb forces; and also, what was particularly interesting, they wanted to know how well equipped and well disciplined the troops were, the troops located at the forward line, and they would draft reports thereof. And I would receive such reports; not only myself, but other members of the staff as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I believe we have clarified the answer that you gave to my colleague from the Prosecution. You also spoke of and you indicated on the map the combat lines that you maintained against Serb forces. And you also responded to a question by Mr. Mundis regarding your positions against HVO forces at the time. Tell us, please, what is exactly the Travnik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was there an HVO brigade in Travnik, and what was its name?

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was an HVO brigade in Travnik which was called Travnicka Brigade. There was another one, speaking of HVO, which was called Frankopani, and that was in the area of Guca Gora. That is where their headquarters were.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, you spoke about the fact that HVO units at one point took position of elevated ground. Tell us, please: Where were the units of the HVO Travnik Brigade located -- rather, deployed in April, May, and June just prior to the outbreak of the conflict, in the town itself and in the area around the town?

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the town itself is concerned, in that context I can mention the former JNA club. That is where they were. That will be the command of the 7th Corps later on, Sebisic. And then I remember they took possession of some premises that had been used by various companies. So this is as far as the staff and the command is concerned. As for the troops, I think that I indicated yesterday that they took possession of high-ground area to the south and to the north of Travnik. I'm referring to the mountain of Vilenica and the southern slopes of Vlasic, in particular, the area of Kajabasa. This was a high area that was not in direct contact with Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, who was deployed at Hajdarove Njive and whether that area also dominated the town of Travnik, whether it was also high ground above the town itself.

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the area located 500 metres from the facility that we saw a moment ago, from the religious school. And it is high ground with respect to the religious school, in military terms. That is the only spot from which one is able to control the religious school.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it possible to control the area of Travnik, the town of Travnik, from these elevated points that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. And as far as Serb forces are concerned, Serb forces that were deployed at Vlasic, that applied to them, too. They were on elevated ground.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Speaking of the confrontation with the HVO, tell us, please, who held the approach road to Travnik from the direction of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was an HVO checkpoint in the area of Dolac on Lasva, which is a junction on the road towards Travnik. And also in the area of Guca Gora.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In connection with that, I should like to know whether at the time of the attack on the town of Travnik, whether the line of confrontation against the HVO stayed in the area that you indicated on the map, or whether these locations, these spots were also part of the confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was referring only to the area in connection with the 312th Brigade. However, to the north and to the east towards Novi Travnik, there were also units of the brigade -- the units which were in contact with HVO forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My learned friend also asked you about possible violations committed by members of your brigade outside the area in which you were militarily active. As far as I understood his question, he wanted to know whether you were aware of any such conduct on the part of your soldiers who were on leave. Yesterday, I showed you a large number of documents in which you requested your troops to come from various locations, Vitez, Mehurici, Zenica, and some others. I would like to know why your men were there at all. How come they were there? And who were they?

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were fighters from the Travnik Municipality, from the military zone of the former TO. And since that area had fallen into Serb hands - I am referring to a large area of the Vlasic plateau and Karaula - most of these villages were either Muslim or Croat villages, and the population was forced to abandon these villages, and they eventually arrived in Travnik. So they were accommodated either in Travnik, in the town of Travnik or in the surrounding villages. So many of these soldiers were from there, and they had their families there. And many of them also went to Zenica and Kakanj to find accommodation there. And whenever they would go back to that area, there would be problems. I spoke about the issues related to the passage of troops and similar.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have barracks in which you were able to accommodate the people who were not residents of Travnik?

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, we didn't have barracks where we could accommodate a platoon or a company, let alone a battalion. There was barracks in the centre of the town, but it was used for accommodation of refugees. And also members of the 17th Krajina Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis asked you a number of questions in connection with the possible participation of your units in combat operations in the greater area of Travnik Municipality. I should like to know in connection with that whether you had a Howitzer in the 312th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where was it? And also where was the crew of that Howitzer?

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had combat positions in Bas Bunar, in that area. And in light of the way this Howitzer was used, it was necessary for it to be there because of the range and the Serb forces. In the area of Biljani, we had -- I don't know the exact location because we didn't have enough men in that area, the area stretching from there to Vlasic plateau. So I cannot recall the exact location of that 105-millimetre Howitzer in the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise for the leading question. But can you please clarify, is that the area where units of the 306th were also active?

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In response to a question about the protection of the population in your zone of combat operations, you said that you took all the necessary measures to protect their houses, et cetera. And you said that you did this because these inhabitants left as they had been threatened by arms. Who had threatened these inhabitants? And we're referring to the Croatian inhabitants of these places.

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Unfortunately that happened at the beginning of June 1993. The inhabitants of Croatian villages were forced to leave.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who forced them?

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: HVO members did. And how do I know this? I know this because many citizens, when they returned later on in 1994 and after the Washington Agreement, they returned and said we went to Vlasic. We were received by the Serbian forces. They took to Kiseljak, et cetera. We were maltreated. We didn't want to go. So such information was provided in conversation with them. And the citizens said that these soldiers forced them to go to the area where there were Serbian forces who took them over and then transferred them to the Kiseljak region.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In connection with a question put to you by the President of the Chamber about your resubordination and in connection with an answer you provided yesterday according to which the OG Bosanska Krajina had a task that wasn't related to the area in question, my question is: Do you have any knowledge as to whether the OG Bosanska Krajina in some -- at some time in 1993 was assigned other tasks? And did you have orders from the 3rd Corps according to which you were to obey orders issued by the OG, by the operation group?

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I had the opportunity of listening to certain activities, to listen to information about the activities of OG, operations group, their task was to form the free men to join brigades so that they could raise the blockade of Sarajevo. What happened happened. Certain activities were carried out that didn't correspond to the main idea, the main plan. So the Bosanska Krajina OG which didn't -- which wasn't linked to the combat zone had the main task of raising the blockade of Sarajevo. And as such, it took upon itself the duty to carry out the activities that were carried out in 1993. This was done because of the impossibility of command and control, because of the impossibility of acting together with the command of us with other brigades who couldn't communicate with OG Zapad. It was impossible for the newly developed situation to be solved.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Caber, you have been shown a video in which you saw on television, too. You recognised the location where it was shot, and you recognised -- you identified two persons. Please tell me, the Territorial Defence staff of which you were a chief at the date that you mentioned, was that TO staff -- did that TO staff establish military power in the municipality? Was it, in fact, the body that had authority to issue orders, or did you have some other kind of tasks? And if so, please tell us what sort of tasks you had.

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence staff didn't have military authority of any kind. When you say "authority," it means that you have a president of the municipality, that you have control over the economy. It means that the people in the municipality were under their authority. But no, this was not the case. They weren't under the staff command. The command of the TO staff had to perform duties at the front lines. They had to engage troops and units. But also in cooperation with the legal authorities, in cooperation with the municipality, they had to ensure that there was logistical support for the combat operations; that is to say, they had to ensure that food was provided.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you said that the HVO was present there and today said that the HVO and the police were present, the HVO and armed forces were present there. Did any of them have weapons? Was the police force armed, or the HVO or the reserve police force? Did they need permission of any kind? Did any of them need to request permission from the TO staff if they wanted to gather in some place in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not from the TO.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If anyone gave permission for people to gather in Travnik, which organ would issue such permission?

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be the wartime presidency in Travnik Municipality, which was headed by the president of the municipality, and it was composed of -- well, I don't know exactly who it was composed of. I just know that the commander of the TO staff wasn't part of that wartime presidency.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After having seen the video, you commented on something that you had seen on television a year or two ago. But my question is at the time, as chief of the staff, did you have any knowledge about who formed the Muslim forces? Do you know who their command was, or did you have any knowledge about how they were organised? As a result of the post that you held, do you have any knowledge of this with regard to those forces that had been formed independently of the TO? Have you understood my question?

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm waiting for the end of the interpretation. But no, I didn't know anything about this. As I told your learned colleague, I didn't know who this -- who composed this formation. Perhaps there were refugees, refugees from Bosanska Krajina. As to the officers, as to the superior-subordinate relationship, no, I don't know. I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also answered a question put to you by my learned colleague by saying that you thought that those -- that later on, after the BH Army had been formed, you thought that these Muslim forces to enter [as interpreted] the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim. My question is do you know whether all of these forces entered and became part of that battalion? Or did just part of these forces entered that battalion? Or would you be able to say which members of those Muslim forces entered the 1st Battalion? Do you know anything about this? Do you personally know anything about this?

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, look, all I know is what I as a soldier always respected. All those who wanted to be under a single command and who wanted to respect orders from a single command, such people were always welcome. And as such, they probably become members, not only of the 1st Battalion of the 7th, I assume that that was the case for the entire BH Army. Your question was perhaps a little more specific. This is a question that was also put to me by the Prosecution. There were also people who were not willing, that -- well, let's say from the area of Bosnia-Herzegovina, but they were not willing to be placed under that command. So I assume these people didn't even become part of the 7th. That is information that I later obtained.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Caber, you also spoke about the attendance of certain meetings at which General Alagic spoke about the groups who refused to be placed under the command. And you also mentioned discussions with members of the international community, and they spoke to you about the existence of these groups. Given what you have just said, you said that after the conflict, you were not in contact with your command. Can you tell us when this occurred. Was it in mid-1993, in the second half of 1993, or in the first half of 1993? Is that when these stories of certain groups of mujahedin were stories that were told to you? Can you go back in time and tell us whether you can remember the period, the time when this occurred?

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the summer of 1993. I really don't know the month. I know that it was in the summer of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since the President of the Trial Chamber mentioned Document P304 and it's not a document we can have a look at right now -- or in fact, we do have the document here. I apologise. But could we show the witness this document that the President of the Chamber referred to so that the witness can tell us about the nature of this document. I would like to ask the usher to show Document P304 to the witness, and we can provide a copy if you can't find one.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before you are shown this document, I would like to ask you another question because you are a member of the military. The units and commands that act or that acted in the area where your unit acted, was it customary for those units to inform you about the action they would take even if they were not subordinated to you or even if you weren't their superiors? Was this customary?

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you have a look at the document now. Is this an order of some kind?

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is a report from the 3rd Corps command on the situation in Travnik. And a reference is made to brigades for communications and linked to the Zapad OG. We can see that this highest command in Travnik because of the impossibility of these units of communicating with OG Zapad undertook the duty to report and establish contact with the units referred to.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You can return the document now.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now be shown another document. And questions were put to the witness in relation to this document. The document in question is Defence Document Number 1155. We have the document here, and it has not yet been admitted into evidence. So perhaps it would be simplest if we showed the witness our document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You could perhaps put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have you had the opportunity of examining the document? You can have a look at it like that. Everyone will be able to see the document on the monitor. What sort of a document is this?

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document in which the commander of the Bosanska Krajina OG is ordering --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are we looking at the same document? Is this an order --

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is an information -- let me just have another look.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please tell me, is this an order or is this some other type of document?

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a piece of information or report according to which the commander of the Bosanska Krajina OG is informing commands in the zone of operations which were linked to the Zapad and Bosanska Krajina OGs. He's informing them about the situation. And above all, about the objective of protecting and taking measures to prevent looting in abandoned villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Since you are a soldier and I am not, can you please tell me whether these two documents, the report we have shown you and this information that you have in front of you which was issued by Commander Mehmed Alagic, can you tell us whether in military terms you can demonstrate anything with regard to the superior-subordinate relationship between the high and low commands. Is there anything that can be concluded on the basis of these documents with regard to subordination?

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Since the command for the Bosanska Krajina OG at the time in question, at the beginning of June, was in the situation it was in, and we know what sort of a situation it was in, they undertook not to remain passive observers, but they undertook to exercise control and to inform units since according to their estimate they should be aware of what their duties were. This seemed to be a professional way of proceeding.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are these documents of an informative kind for the units in that area, or are they documents that demonstrate the way in which command was performed for the units referred to here?

utterances.speaker: ZIJAD CABER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, look, it's both informative, but it also requests that commands take certain measures and carry out certain tasks. So it contains elements of both of these things. Information is provided and tasks are also assigned.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Caber.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no other questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll turn to the other Defence team now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We only have -- we have only one question for Mr. Caber.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: And it relates to a question put by Ms. Residovic. It has to do with the Muslim forces that you mentioned, the Muslim forces that were present in the Travnik region up until the time of the formation of the brigades in the corps. If I told you that certain members of the Muslim forces joined units other than the 7th Brigade 1st Battalion and units that were placed under the command of the 3rd Corps, for example the 306th Brigade, the 17th Krajina Brigade, and the 307th Brigade, you would probably agree with me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. That was the only question I had for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I just wanted to ask whether once you have finished with your questions, once we have finished with the witness, whether it would be the right time to address the issue of documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Witness, this concludes your examination. You have been here for two days and answered numerous and various questions. You have answered the questions put to you by the Prosecution, by the Defence, and by the Chamber. Thank you for your testimony. We wish you a good trip home, and we wish you all the best in your post in the Ministry of Defence. I will now ask the witness to escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have some documents to deal with. I believe that the Prosecution would also like to tender the map into evidence. But Defence counsel may take the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the documents that we have provided the Prosecution, the Trial Chamber has also been following the documents we have shown to the witness. We suggest that all these documents be admitted evidence as Defence exhibits, from 1 to 26 -- the documents 1 to 26, documents that the witness identified as documents that he himself drafted, or documents that his brigade drafted, or that he as commander of the 312th Brigade received. So given that the witness has identified the documents and he has spoken about the contents of these various documents, we believe that all the conditions have been met for these documents to be admitted into evidence. The witness also identified all the documents referred to under part A, Combat Report. These documents are documents 1 to 9. He identified them as documents which were combat-related reports, regular and irregular reports, and his command forwarded them to him at times and in the manner indicated in these documents. They were regular and interim reports. And the witness in the course of his testimony also mentioned various events referred to in these documents. For these reasons, Defence counsel suggests that all these documents be admitted into evidence. And finally, under Section B entitled "Movement," we have documents identified by the witness as documents that he drafted himself or as documents that his chief of staff or battalion commander drafted. He had a -- examined a significant number of the documents, and he has testified in detail about the events referred to in the documents. He was also shown a document in which the HVO responds to his requests, and he identified the facts in the document he was shown, that it was a document that was a response to his request. Since this witness is familiar with the documents and since the witness spoke about the facts related in these documents in answers to questions put to him, we believe that all the conditions have been met for all the documents under the title "Movement," documents 1 to 26, be accepted as -- be admitted into evidence. Under Section 2 entitled "The HVO," the Defence referred to six documents, five of which -- four of which were shown to the witness. The witness hasn't seen the documents before, but he was familiar with the facts related in each of those documents. He knew who the people were who had been appointed to posts within the parallel organs of power in Travnik. He insisted on the fact that they were the only legitimate organs of power and that parallel judiciary organs were established. And he also mentioned that the document on number 4 referred to facts according to which the conflict in Novi Travnik in 1992 were not provoked by the Armija, by the army, but by the HVO. The witness wasn't shown documents under number 5 and 6, but the witness did testify about some facts related in these documents. In fact, he said that he knew that on the 8th of April in Travnik, there was a meeting of HVO representatives, and Dario Kordic, among others, attended it. And with regard to the events that followed -- and he also spoke about the events in which two of his soldiers were killed. Given that the documents under 5 and 6 relate to those events, I believe that we have good reason to have these documents admitted into evidence. And this is also valid for documents 1 to 4. For these reasons, the Defence suggest that all these documents be admitted into evidence. Could they be admitted under these numbers. And in accordance with the Chamber's order, we will provide for the purposes of identification all the documents that we have on our complete list of documents. This will enable us to maintain the same number on the document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, your observations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Trial Chamber admits into evidence all the documents contain in the binder, and there is a list of these documents contained at the beginning of the binder. For the BH, we have 26 documents; combat reports, 9 documents; under movement, there are 21 documents; under HVO, there are 6 documents. I'd like to point out for the sake of the transcript that the document under the title "BH" number 4, Document 613, this is a typing error in the English version because the name of General Enver Hadzihasanovic -- well, we have an address email which is indicated, and at the time there was no email. So instead of typing Z, we have an email address. It's a slight typing error. Nothing escapes the Trial Chamber's attention. I wanted to point this out. Mr. Registrar, you will have to give us numbers for these documents. Perhaps not tonight because this involves a lot of work. Perhaps tomorrow you will provide us with the relevant numbers. Mr. Mundis -- yes, I will give the floor to Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence would like to ask the Chamber for one additional decision. We have invited three to four witnesses for this week. As a result of the problems that have arisen in the meantime, and because we had a BH Army officer as a witness for the first time, that examination took longer than expected. As we indicated, the second witness, Mr. Siljak, who was a member of the municipal staff of the defence and then throughout 1993 he was the chief of staff of the 306th Brigade, he's a witness that we scheduled for two days. And I believe that it is the interest of Tribunal and the Defence of our client and in the interests of truth that we should not shorten the examination of that witness. So we, therefore, suggest that he be the first witness and not Witness Mesanovic. I'm referring to the next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're telling us that the witness who had to arrived on Friday will be examined next week because the second witness will need two days because of the fact that he occupied a certain position in the 306th Brigade. Very well. We can only agree with your suggestion because then that will be the witness for next week. We were asking ourselves who the witnesses would be. We have the session on Tuesday afternoon, because Monday is a holiday. Then also Wednesday afternoon, Thursday afternoon, and also we wanted to know whether there would be a session or Friday or not. On the table of the Registrar, there was an empty courtroom due to technical reasons. So does that mean that there will be no session on Friday afternoon, or is it maybe possible to schedule a session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So it seems there cannot be any hearing on Friday afternoon in this courtroom due to technical reasons. Mr. Mundis, we still have several minutes for the map which is on your left.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. With the leave of the Trial Chamber and perhaps if there are no objections from the Defence, what the Prosecution would propose doing is marking this map for identification, and then allowing subsequent witnesses to make further markings on that map, perhaps using different coloured markers. That way we don't have 10 or 12 versions of this map with different units marked on there. That's what we would propose, unless there are objections to that. So we would mark it for identification for now, and subsequent witnesses could use different coloured pens or we can address that issue as we go. But just to keep the fewer number of maps that come in as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The only technical question is will we have enough various coloured felt tips, because if there are 10 or 12 witnesses we will need 12 colours. We are familiar with primary colours, but we will require perhaps secondary colours. If Defence counsel has no objections to raise, we'll mark this for identification, which means that the map could be used, providing we use various colours. Mr. Registrar, could we have a number marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document will be marked for identification under number P930.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Are there any other issues that the Defence would like to raise? No. The Prosecution? No comments. We had planned to have the hearing tomorrow in the morning instead of in the afternoon. But apparently that might cause a number of problems. So we will have the hearing tomorrow in the afternoon. It will commence at 2.15, and I will see everyone in this courtroom tomorrow at 2.15. We will now adjourn, and we will resume at 2.15. Thank you.
